subject: Compliance evidence sprint: scheduling, gap list, and escalations
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
To: BrightPath Compliance <audits@brightpath.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Compliance evidence sprint: scheduling, gap list, and escalations

Hi team,

Following up from our kickoff call — attaching the first draft of the control mapping and an initial evidence request grid (control-mapping-v1.xlsx). BrightPath, thanks again for the outline you sent; I tried to map our current artifacts to the ISO 27001 / FedRAMP scoping you shared.

As we prepare for the sampling window, two asks to start:
- Can BrightPath confirm preferred audit-sampling windows in October vs. late November? We have a product feature freeze Nov 30–Dec 7 that may block some control owners.
- Kimberly & Mina: please review the mapping and flag any controls with missing primary evidence (logs, configs, attestation) — mark owner + urgency in the spreadsheet.

A couple of notes on scope and dependencies:
- FedRAMP readiness: we will need architecture-level evidence for network segmentation + KMS/HSM key rotation records (BrightPath asked for rotation logs for last 12 months).
- ISO 27001: evidence for risk treatment decisions and the current Statement of Applicability (SoA) needs sign-off.

I copied Helix Labs SRE because a few controls reference their integration (SAML assertions, inbound/outbound rules). If Helix can confirm retention windows for their audit logs that would help narrow sampling.

Timeline proposal:
- Week of Sep 27: evidence validation sprint (internal only)
- Oct 11–15: preferred audit sampling window (subject to BrightPath confirming)
- Nov 30–Dec 7: product freeze (avoid scheduling evidence collection)

Please add questions directly to the spreadsheet and reply with availability constraints.

Thanks,
Aditya
Aditya Rao
Senior Manager, GRC Programs
Redwood Inference

Attachments: control-mapping-v1.xlsx (spreadsheet, 32kb)
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, BrightPath Compliance <audits@brightpath.com>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Sep 2026 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Compliance evidence sprint: scheduling, gap list, and escalations

Aditya — thanks for kicking this off and for the clear asks. A few quick points after skimming the mapping:

- I can lead SOC 2 / continuous monitoring artifacts (alerts, SIEM retention claim). I'll update the sheet with the owners and the preliminary evidence types I know we have (SIEM export, alert config snapshots).
- For FedRAMP KMS/HSM: we do have key rotation logs but they live in the secure audit bucket. I'll add a note and link to the architecture diagram (sc-architecture-diagram.pdf) showing where KMS sits in our infra.
- Availability: Oct 11–15 mostly works for me, but Oct 13 I am onsite for a vendor review; can be remote for evidence calls. Late November is risky because of the planned release.

Two asks from my side:
1) Can BrightPath confirm whether they need raw SIEM exports or summarized exports with JSON schema? That changes how much prep we need.
2) Mina — can you check the SoA sign-off owner? I think product legal still needs to sign one control exception.

Thanks — attaching the architecture diagram reference for context.

Kimberly Park
Director, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Attachments: sc-architecture-diagram.pdf (PDF, 1.2MB)

From: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
Cc: BrightPath Compliance <audits@brightpath.com>, Helix Labs SRE <sre@helixlabs.com>
Date: Wed, 22 Sep 2026 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Compliance evidence sprint: scheduling, gap list, and escalations

Thanks — I reviewed the mapping and added a gap list tab in the spreadsheet. A few highlights:

- Evidence missing for Control A.9.2 (access provisioning): we do not have a clean export showing joiner/mover/leaver activity for a 6-month window. Owner: sec-ops (TBD).
- Control A.12.4 (logging & monitoring): SIEM exports exist but the retention policy doc is out of date; I attached an evidence-request-template.docx with suggested wording for the retention artefact.
- Exception: There is an outstanding exception for feature-flagged telemetry where we relied on sampling; product legal asked for a compensating control. I flagged this as high priority because it may affect evidence acceptance for ISO sampling.

Helix SRE — can you confirm whether your ELB logs are retained for 90 days? That affects our FedRAMP sample for network ingress controls.

I propose we run a 3-day internal evidence collection sprint Sep 27–29 to triage and assign owners, then hand off to BrightPath for sampling prep in the Oct window.

Mina Haddad
Head of Compliance Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments: evidence-request-template.docx (DOCX, 18kb)

From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>

Date: Wed, 22 Sep 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Compliance evidence sprint: scheduling, gap list, and escalations

Kimberly / Mina — great updates, thanks. Quick executive summary and next steps so we have a single source of truth: 

Summary:
- Internal evidence sprint: Sep 27–29 (internal owners triage + collect)
- Proposed external sampling: Oct 11–15 (pending BrightPath confirmation)
- Avoid evidence requests during product freeze Nov 30–Dec 7

Critical gaps (owners assigned where known):
- Access provisioning exports (Owner: sec-ops — action: export + validation by Sep 29)
- SIEM retention statement (Owner: Kimberly — action: update retention doc + attach SIEM export sample by Sep 28)
- Feature-flag telemetry exception (Owner: Product Legal — action: provide compensating control or accept exception by Oct 4)

Escalation path: If any owner cannot provide items by the internal sprint cutoff, escalate to me and Mina by email with the reason and expected delivery date. We will use the HubSpot deal HLX-4421 to track missing evidence actions (link above).

BrightPath — please confirm whether Oct 11–15 works and whether you need raw SIEM exports or summarized extracts (Kim asked this question as well). Also confirm whether you will require photo-stamped attachments for any physical evidence (e.g., locked server racks) — we currently expect no on-prem servers for this scope.

I'll update the sheet with the sprint checklists and owners by EOD today.

Thanks,
Aditya
